subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we stay aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Pain points we heard:
- Unit economics: model inference costs are a material line item as you scale to 10s of millions of requests/month.
- Variability: production traffic has spiky peaks which drive unpredictable burst costs.
- Accuracy vs cost trade-offs: you need to maintain current QA thresholds (F1/latency) but reduce per-request spend.

Current stack:
- Frontend + microservices on AWS (us-west-2)
- GPUs: in-house p3 and mixed on-demand instances for inference today
- Model: in-house tuned variant of an open LLM for summarization and routing

Success criteria (what you said):
1) Reduce per-1000-request cost by ~30% without degrading key fidelity metrics (summary ROUGE/F1).
2) Keep 99th-percentile latency under 450ms for interactive flows.
3) Support burst capacity up to 3x sustained throughput with predictable spend.

What we propose next (action items):
- Ben/Marissa: send our cost-modeling template so your infra team can fill current unit costs and traffic profile (attached).
- Alex: share a representative traffic trace and a small set of evaluation prompts (anonymized) so we can run an initial projection and cost/vs-quality analysis.
- Procurement: we'll prepare an initial canary pricing worksheet and a short SOW for Dedicated capacity if you want reserved pricing.

Technical knobs we discussed and Redwood stance:
- Batching & adaptive batching: we can improve throughput during high-concurrency windows; need traffic trace.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context patterns — often reduces token count by 10-40% on chat-style flows.
- Quantization: we recommended trying 8-bit/4-bit quantization profiles; open to model-specific experiments depending on your quality tolerance.

Attachments: redwood-cost-modeling-template.xlsx (please fill and return)

Next meeting suggestion:
- 30–45 minute technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineering team next week to review trace + initial projections.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the template. Thanks — sensible progress here.

Best,
Ben Carter
